subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrocarbons
summary: Alkanes (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, sp³) are fairly unreactive and undergo free-radical substitution. Their conformations (staggered vs eclipsed ethane) differ in energy.
Alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ, C=C) and alkynes (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, C≡C) undergo electrophilic addition. HX adds by Markovnikov's rule, except HBr with peroxide (anti-Markovnikov). Alkenes show geometrical isomerism.
Terminal alkynes are weakly acidic (sp carbon) and form acetylides. Ozonolysis tells where the double bond was.
Benzene is aromatic (planar, cyclic, 6 π electrons — Hückel 4n + 2). It prefers electrophilic substitution, and substituents direct incoming groups to ortho/para or meta positions.

formulas.name: Wurtz reaction
formulas.note: Gives mixtures with two different alkyl halides; can't make methane.

formulas.name: Kolbe's electrolysis
formulas.when: Alkanes with an even number of carbons.

formulas.name: Free-radical halogenation
formulas.formula: CH₄ + Cl₂ (hν) → CH₃Cl + HCl (initiation, propagation, termination)
formulas.note: Reactivity of halogens: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; 3° H is replaced fastest.

formulas.name: Markovnikov addition
formulas.note: H goes to the carbon that already has more H (more stable carbocation forms).

formulas.name: Peroxide (Kharasch) effect
formulas.mistake: Works only with HBr — not with HCl or HI.

formulas.name: Ozonolysis
formulas.formula: R₂C=CR′₂ + O₃ then Zn/H₂O → R₂C=O + O=CR′₂

formulas.name: Hydrogenation of alkynes
formulas.formula: Lindlar's catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃, quinoline) → cis-alkene;  Na in liquid NH₃ → trans-alkene

formulas.name: Hydration of alkynes
formulas.formula: HC≡CH + H₂O (HgSO₄, dil. H₂SO₄) → CH₃CHO;  other alkynes → ketones

formulas.name: Acidity of hydrocarbons
formulas.when: Why terminal alkynes react with Na, NaNH₂ and ammoniacal AgNO₃.

formulas.name: Aromaticity (Hückel rule)
formulas.formula: planar + cyclic + fully conjugated + (4n + 2) π electrons
formulas.note: Cyclopentadienyl anion (6π) is aromatic; the cation (4π) is not.

formulas.name: Electrophilic substitution of benzene
formulas.formula: nitration (HNO₃/H₂SO₄, NO₂⁺);  halogenation (X₂/FeX₃);  sulphonation (fuming H₂SO₄);  Friedel–Crafts alkylation (RX/AlCl₃) and acylation (RCOCl/AlCl₃)

formulas.name: Directive influence
formulas.formula: o/p-directing activating: –OH, –NH₂, –OR, –CH₃;  o/p-directing deactivating: halogens;  m-directing deactivating: –NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COOH, –SO₃H
formulas.when: Predicting where the next group goes.
formulas.note: Halogens are the odd case: deactivating (−I) yet ortho/para-directing (+R).

examples.title: Ozonolysis product
examples.solution: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ splits at the double bond → 2 CH₃CHO (ethanal).

examples.title: Markovnikov vs peroxide
examples.problem: Propene + HBr, with and without benzoyl peroxide?
examples.solution: Without peroxide: 2-bromopropane (Markovnikov, via 2° carbocation). With peroxide: 1-bromopropane (free-radical, anti-Markovnikov).

examples.title: cis or trans
examples.problem: But-2-yne is reduced with H₂/Lindlar's catalyst and separately with Na/liq. NH₃. Products?

examples.title: Is it aromatic?
examples.problem: Which are aromatic: benzene, cyclooctatetraene, cyclopentadienyl anion, cyclobutadiene?
examples.solution: Benzene (6π) and cyclopentadienyl anion (6π) obey 4n + 2. Cyclooctatetraene (8π, non-planar) and cyclobutadiene (4π, antiaromatic) are not.

examples.title: Nitration of toluene
examples.solution: –CH₃ is activating and o/p-directing → o-nitrotoluene and p-nitrotoluene (p major due to less crowding).

examples.title: Friedel–Crafts acylation
examples.solution: Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃). The acylium ion CH₃C≡O⁺ is the electrophile; unlike alkylation there is no rearrangement and no polysubstitution.

topics.title: Conformations of ethane
topics.explain: Rotation about the C–C single bond gives staggered (most stable, minimum torsional strain) and eclipsed (least stable) conformations; the energy difference is only ~12.5 kJ/mol, so they interconvert rapidly. Shown with Newman and sawhorse projections.

topics.title: Geometrical isomerism
topics.explain: Restricted rotation about C=C allows cis and trans isomers when each double-bonded carbon has two different groups. cis-But-2-ene has a higher boiling point (polar); trans has a higher melting point (packs better).

topics.title: Preparation of alkenes
topics.explain: Dehydration of alcohols (conc. H₂SO₄, heat), dehydrohalogenation of alkyl halides (alcoholic KOH — Saytzeff product, the more substituted alkene, is major), and partial reduction of alkynes.

topics.title: Reactions of alkenes
topics.explain: Addition of H₂, X₂ (Br₂ water decolourises — test for unsaturation), HX, H₂O (acid-catalysed); oxidation with cold dilute alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent, diol; purple colour lost); ozonolysis; polymerisation (polythene).

topics.title: Alkynes
topics.explain: Prepared from calcium carbide (CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂) or by double dehydrohalogenation. Terminal alkynes give white precipitates with ammoniacal AgNO₃ — a test distinguishing them from alkenes. Ethyne polymerises to benzene in a red-hot iron tube.

topics.title: Benzene structure
topics.explain: Kekulé structures are resonance forms; all C–C bonds are equal (139 pm, between single and double). Benzene resists addition because it would lose aromatic stabilisation.

topics.title: Carcinogenicity and toxicity
topics.explain: Many polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (from incomplete combustion of coal, tobacco) are carcinogenic, e.g. 1,2-benzanthracene.

ratta: Markovnikov: H to carbon with more H;  peroxide effect only with HBr.
